eligibility.evidence: Overview of study, Results: ChatGPT retells 116 stories in chains of three using the same instructions as the human serial-reproduction study; paradigm cites Bartlett (ref 10) and Breithaupt et al. 2022 (ref 29); word, concept and affect outcomes analysed against human retellings.

A.title: Humans create more novelty than ChatGPT when asked to retell a story

paradigms.name: Serial reproduction of narratives (three-step retelling chains)
paradigms.location: Overview of study; stories are the 116 from Study 1 of ref 29

D.population: Amazon Mechanical Turk retellers (data of Breithaupt et al. 2022); emotion raters 537 AMT (humans) and 531 Prolific (ChatGPT retellings)
D.metric: word count, part-of-speech proportions, synset novelty and survival, age of acquisition, rated happiness and sadness

effects.label: SUPER-NORMATIVE
effects.location: Fig 2 and Discussion: humans create 55-60% novel synsets per retelling, ChatGPT makes few changes after retelling 1; Fig 1 regression p<0.001 for shallower decline. Affect preservation (Fig 4) is equivalent in both and not coded as a second row

E.headline: Humans keep inventing new concepts across retellings while ChatGPT summarises once and then repeats itself; both preserve emotional ratings.

G.notes: One closed model (ChatGPT3), version, date and sampling settings unreported; one prompt, no variants. Human data come from an earlier study with different rater pools (AMT vs Prolific). Outcome fits no standard kind cleanly: coded as effect (novelty drift) with emotion stability similar in both. Contamination not discussed.
